transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because my primary doctor seems pretty concerned about my eating habits. She thinks my meal planning has gotten a bit too tight lately. Honestly, to me, it just feels like I'm keeping things orderly. I usually just have a yogurt for breakfast, and if work gets busy, I'll skip lunch. Then for dinner, I just make sure it's very measured. It just helps keep the day structured, but she felt I needed to come in and talk about it.
Do you ever feel a strong fear of gaining weight or do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives after eating?

I don't ever make myself sick or use laxatives, no. I've never done anything like that. But... yes, I suppose I do have a strong fear of gaining weight. 

For me, it's really about the numbers. If I step on the scale and it's up even a single pound—like after a normal dinner or if I had to eat a restaurant meal—I feel this sharp panic. It just feels like I've completely lost control of things, and I immediately feel like I need to correct it the next day to get the numbers back where they belong.
Do you feel that your body weight or shape has a strong impact on how you see yourself or how you feel about yourself?

Yes, it definitely does. I know I'm an older woman now, and I'm not trying to look like I'm in my twenties or anything like that. But I still judge how well I'm handling myself by how I look. If my waist and hips look contained in my clothes, I feel like I'm doing okay. If they don't, I feel like I'm failing. It's just a very direct measure of my self-discipline for me.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently, or do you feel that your perception of your body weight or shape is inaccurate?

Well, yes, I suppose I have lost some weight recently. My primary doctor pointed out that my weight has drifted down a bit more than she likes, which is why she sent me here. 

But as for my perception being inaccurate... I don't really think it is. It's just that, when I look at the chart, I still find myself thinking that a little lower would be a cleaner, more manageable number for me to maintain.
When you say you've lost some weight recently, was this weight loss something you were intentionally trying to achieve through restricting food or increasing control over your eating?

Well, yes, I suppose it is intentional. I actually came in because my primary doctor seems concerned that my meal planning has gotten too tight. But to me, it doesn't really feel like I'm doing anything extreme. 

It just feels like... well, keeping breakfast to a yogurt, skipping lunch if I’m busy, and then making a very measured dinner. It's just a way to make sure the day stays orderly. I like having that structure and control over what I'm taking in, even if it means the scale goes down a bit as a result.
Can you tell me approximately how much weight you’ve lost recently, and whether you think your current weight is lower than what would be considered healthy for someone your height and age?

I've lost, I'd say, about 15 pounds over the last six months or so. 

As for whether it's lower than what's healthy... well, when my primary physician talks about my weight being medically unsafe, part of me really thinks she’s overstating it. I mean, I’m still working, I'm running my errands, and I'm managing my own life just fine. It's hard for me to see it as this serious health issue she makes it out to be when I'm still getting everything done every day without any real problems.
Do you feel that your efforts to control your eating and weight are related to a fear of becoming fat or to a belief that you are overweight, even when others might not see it that way?

Well, I wouldn't say I think I'm overweight right now, but... yes, there is definitely a fear of gaining it back. Or just gaining, period. 

It's more about the numbers and the control. Like, if I step on the scale and it's up even a single pound—maybe after I had a normal dinner or, you know, went to a restaurant—I just feel this... this sharp panic. It feels like I've completely lost control of things. And when that happens, I just immediately feel like I have to correct it the very next day by tightening up my eating again. So, yes, I suppose the fear of the number going up is a big part of it.

Have your concerns about food, weight, or control caused you any problems in your daily life, such as difficulty concentrating, trouble participating in social activities, or problems with work or relationships?

Well, I still keep up with my analysis work just fine. And my errands, like I mentioned earlier. It hasn't caused problems with my concentration or anything like that. 

But... I suppose it has affected things socially a bit. I’ve mostly stopped joining my friends for meals after our book club. Going out to eat at a restaurant just throws off the plan I rely on for the day. It's much easier for me to just head home instead so I can stick to my routine. So, yes, I guess it has changed how I participate in things like that.
Can you tell me approximately what your weight has been in the past, and how your current weight compares to what you consider a normal or healthy weight for someone your height and age?

Well, for most of my adult life, my weight was pretty steady... right around where it was before I lost those 15 pounds I mentioned earlier. So it has drifted down more than my doctor likes recently. She tells me it's below what's considered normal for my height and age. 

But honestly, when I look at the chart myself, I don't see it the same way she does. I actually still find myself thinking that a little lower would be a cleaner, more manageable number. It just feels more precise and easier to maintain in my head, even if she disagrees with me about what's healthy.
Do you feel that your weight or shape influences how you see yourself, even if others don’t seem to notice or agree with your view?

Yes, I suppose it does. I mean, I know I'm an older woman. I'm not trying to look like a teenager or anything like that. But... I still judge how well I'm handling myself by how I look. 

It's more about feeling... contained, I guess. If I put on my clothes and my waist and hips look neat and contained, I feel like I'm doing okay. Like I have things under control. If things feel tight or look different, it bothers me, regardless of what anyone else thinks or says. So, yes, how my shape looks in my clothes definitely influences how I feel about myself.
Would you say your current weight is below what most people would consider a minimally normal weight for someone your height and age?

Well, my doctor definitely thinks so. She tells me it's medically unsafe. But... I don't really see it that way. I mean, part of me thinks she's overstating it, honestly. I'm still doing my analysis work, running my errands, and managing my whole life just fine. If it were really that unsafe, I wouldn't be able to do all of those things, would I? So, yes, it's below what she considers normal, but I don't think it's as bad as she makes it out to be.
Is your desire to keep your weight low mainly driven by a desire to be thin, or is it more about avoiding the feeling of losing control when the scale goes up?

I think it's much more about the control. I don't really care about being thin just for the sake of being thin. 

But... if I step on the scale and it's up even a single pound, like after a normal dinner or going out to a restaurant, I feel this sharp panic. It just hits me that I've lost control of things. And when that happens, I feel like I absolutely have to correct it the very next day to get everything back in order.
